messages:
alex: Heads-up: customer reported OAuth signin failures via GitHub and Google. They see a generic error after provider redirects back. Ticket #CD-9876.

emma: Customer flow: click sign-in -> provider consent -> redirect back -> error page. They pasted network errors: `POST /oauth/token 400 invalid_grant` and our logs show `state_not_found` and `pkce_verification_failed`.

sarah: Can we get the raw callback URL (query params) and the redirect_uri configured on the provider? suspect mismatch between registered redirect_uri and actual redirect target (trailing slash, path rewrite, or casing).

alex: Customer supplied logs. Snippet from our auth-service:
```
[2026-03-15T11:12:05Z] auth-service: incoming /oauth/callback; provider=github; state=st_9x2
[2026-03-15T11:12:05Z] session-store: lookup cookie sid=abcd123 -> not found
[2026-03-15T11:12:05Z] oauth: token exchange failed: invalid_grant
[2026-03-15T11:12:05Z] oauth: pkce_mismatch expected=sha256:AAA got=sha256:BBB
```
They also noted their GitHub app redirect URI is `https://app.example.com/auth/callback` but browser returned to `https://app.example.com/auth/callback/?flow=oauth` (query added + trailing slash).

mike: Recent SPA router change (v2.4) auto-appends trailing slash to canonicalize routes; our PKCE verifier is stored in session (cookie). If provider redirects to a different path, and the cookie is SameSite=Lax/Strict, it might not be sent on the callback -> session missing -> state not found.

emma: Also seen with Google where the provider returns state intact but PKCE verifier mismatch because app regenerates code_verifier on full page reload or loses localStorage. Customer dev said they store code_verifier in localStorage.

sarah: Two buckets: (A) session/cookie lost due to SameSite or path mismatch; (B) code_verifier lost/changed due to SPA full reload or reverse-proxy canonicalization. Need to collect reproduction data: network waterfall with redirects, full callback URL, cookie presence.

alex: Requested customer to try these quick checks: 1) test changing registered redirect_uri to include the trailing slash, 2) try incognito to bypass extensions/cookies, 3) capture browser network trace and console, 4) attempt token exchange with curl using the code + code_verifier.

customer (via ticket): tried adding trailing slash to registered redirect URI -> immediately worked for some users. Incognito didn't fix for others. They have a CDN/edge that rewrites URLs and normalizes slashes.

mike: Proposed fix: normalize incoming callback path before session/PKCE lookup (strip or add trailing slash canonicalization) and tolerate minor differences when matching state keys. I'll put up a small patch to auth-service to attempt both raw and normalized keys.

sarah: Longer term: persist code_verifier keyed to state in our DB (not solely in ephemeral cookie/localStorage) to resist cookie loss and router canonicalization. Also add more logging on state values and incoming code_challenge for debugging.

infra-bot: deploy request created: change-id=GH-4620 oauth-callback-tolerant-lookup; target=canary; owner=mike

mike: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/803 — implements callback normalization and fallback lookup. Rolling to canary now.

infra-bot: canary deploy started. healthcheck: pending.

emma: Meanwhile support checklist to triage with customers:
- Confirm exact redirect_uri registered with provider and the actual callback URL observed (include query string).
- Check for trailing slash or path rewrite at CDN/proxy level.
- Inspect cookie attributes (SameSite, Secure, Domain, Path) to ensure session cookie sent on cross-site redirect.
- Verify where code_verifier is stored (localStorage vs cookie vs server DB) and whether full reload clears it.
- Try manual token exchange with curl to see provider error body.
- Ask for browser and version (Chrome changes to SameSite in M80 caused many regressions).

sarah: internal repro: created a minimal SPA that stores code_verifier in localStorage and applied router auto-slash. Confirmed state lost when redirect path differed, and token exchange failed with invalid_grant. With patch applied, callback succeeds for both variants.

infra-bot: canary deploy successful, healthchecks green.

mike: Rolling patch to production in 10m.

alex: Customer updated: after we changed provider redirect to include trailing slash, their users could sign in. We told them we'll deploy fix to accept both forms and follow up with a root-cause summary.

sarah: Post-deploy tasks: 1) add integration tests for PKCE flows with canonicalization variants, 2) update docs and onboarding guide to call out redirect URI exactness and recommended cookie settings, 3) create ticket to store PKCE verifier server-side to reduce fragility.

emma: I'll close customer ticket once prod deploy finishes and send a short support write-up they can paste in their team's changelog.

mike: Prod deploy finished, monitoring shows no regressions.

alex: Closing thread. root cause: redirect_uri canonicalization + session/code_verifier storage fragility. participants: alex, emma, sarah, mike, infra-bot.
